messages.author: 27aaf64cb2093545
messages.subject: syntax highlighting in knitr/Rnw documents
parts:
In Rnw documents that combine latex and R code it is frequently necessary (or convenient) to refer
to objects with the R/S convention A$x but this seems to wreck havoc with syntax highlighting since
from a latex perspective there are unmatched $$. I've been wondering whether there is a way to
overcome this, since such offending objects only occur in R code chunks or Sexpr expressions.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: syntax highlighting in knitr/Rnw documents
parts: This was a bug, and it was just solved by Johannes Ranke, the maintainer of syntax/rnoweb.vim. See: https://github.com/jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime/pull/8

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: syntax highlighting in knitr/Rnw documents
parts:
It should work for you too if you could delete all syntax/rnoweb.vim scripts from your 'runtimepath' and copy the new version from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime/master/syntax/rnoweb.vim to /usr/shave/vim/vim74/syntax/rnoweb.vim (the correct path depends on your Vim installation). The following command will show your 'runtimepath':

:echo runtimepath?

However, depending on how old your Vim is, the new script might not work as expected.  I tested here with Vim (7.4.712 and the development version) and with Neovim (development version).
